intro: Hong Kong's home cuisine prizes freshness and 'wok hei': yum cha, roast meats, wonton noodles and the cha chaan teng's East-meets-West comfort food.
flavours: Soy sauce, oyster sauce, ginger, spring onion, dried seafood, char siu glaze
hk: You live with this one: the useful skill is explaining it to visitors and naming dishes in English at yum cha.

dishes.name: Har gow
dishes.what: Translucent shrimp dumplings with at least seven pleats, the test of a dim sum chef.

dishes.name: Siu mai
dishes.what: Open-topped pork and prawn dumplings, often topped with crab roe or carrot.

dishes.name: Char siu bao
dishes.what: Fluffy steamed buns bursting open around sweet barbecued pork.

dishes.name: Cheung fun
dishes.what: Silky steamed rice-sheet rolls with prawns, beef or char siu, in sweet soy.

dishes.name: Char siu
dishes.what: Sticky-sweet barbecued pork with red edges, hung in roast-meat shop windows.

dishes.name: Roast goose
dishes.what: Crisp-skinned roast goose with plum sauce; Yat Lok and Kam's made it famous.

dishes.name: Wonton noodles
dishes.what: Springy egg noodles and shrimp wontons in a shrimp-roe broth, served small.

dishes.name: Claypot rice
dishes.what: Rice cooked in a clay pot over fire with Chinese sausage or chicken; scrape up the crispy bottom.

dishes.name: Egg tart
dishes.what: Cha chaan teng custard tart with shortcrust or flaky pastry; Tai Cheong's are famous.

dishes.name: Pineapple bun
dishes.what: Sweet bun with a crackly sugary top (no pineapple); with a slab of butter it's bo lo yau.

dishes.name: Hong Kong milk tea
dishes.what: Strong black tea strained through a 'silk stocking' and mixed with evaporated milk.

dishes.name: Egg waffle
dishes.what: Bubble-shaped street waffle, crisp outside and chewy inside.
